subject: Request: TTF & sustained token-rate carve-out for streaming vs sync endpoints
messages:
From: Alice Cheng <alice@concordhealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.procure@concordhealth.com>, legal@concordhealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Streaming behaviour: TTF & sustained tokens — exception request

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Concord Health is close to finalizing the pilot contract, but our compliance and clinical vendors require an explicit runtime commitment for live transcription workflows. Two specific asks we need Redwood to approve as an amendment to the hosted SLA:

- Time-to-first-token (TTF) for streaming endpoints must be <= 250ms measured 95th percentile for 1–4 sentence utterances.
- Sustained token throughput must be >= 45 tokens/sec (end-to-end, per connection) for multi-turn interactive sessions; we understand this may be met with a non-streaming fallback but need a clear behavior.

These requirements are driven by our clinical transcription latency (real-time triage) and downstream monitor integrations. Can Redwood agree to a scoped exception/commitment for the production workspace for the DH-4093 pilot? If so we will route an internal procurement approval quickly.

Attachments: sample_latency_chart.csv (attached by Concord)

Best,
Alice Cheng
Program Manager, Clinical Ops
Concord Health

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Alice Cheng <alice@concordhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Streaming behaviour: TTF & sustained tokens — exception request

Alice — thanks for the clear ask and the chart.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I attached our internal SLA-exception intake form so we capture scope and the relevant workspace IDs.
- Looping in Rishi (commercial) to align on contract language and pricing impact.
- I’ll ask Product/Infra for a preliminary feasibility + monitoring plan; we usually need a canary for 2 weeks before committing to anything in the hosted SLA.

Two clarifying Qs for your team:
1) Is the 45 tok/s requirement per user session or per tenant?
2) Do you need the TTF requirement for all model classes or only for our low-latency curated models?

I’ve attached: sla-exception-intake-form.pdf (internal), and a draft amendment template we can populate.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Concord TTF/token-rate request — commercial framing

Team — flagging DH-4093 as it looks like it will require a scoped SLA carve-out and price uplift. Initial thoughts:

- Technical posture: infra can likely meet TTF <=250ms p95 for 1–4 sentence utterances on our curated low-latency model family if we reserve dedicated pools and enable aggressive batching/pinning. Sustained 45 tok/s per connection is achievable but will need explicit connection-level rate guarantees (and will reduce multi-tenant throughput).
- Commercial impact: propose a monthly dedicated-reservation fee + usage uplift (~20–35%) for the carve-out, plus a monitoring/observability surcharge.
- Execution: require a canary (2 weeks), synthetic probes, and 30-day rollback window. Product wants a playbook for failover to non-streaming sync endpoint with deterministic token-rate expectations.

I’ll draft a short amendment and an internal cost estimate. Vanessa — can you confirm Concord’s answer to the two clarifying Qs? Lauren — will need quick legal/commercial signoff on the amendment template.

-Rishi

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:15:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: Concord TTF/token-rate request — commercial framing

Thanks — I’m okay approving a provisional exception given the pilot nature, subject to the following:

- Product/Infra written signoff on the canary plan (metrics, probes, rollback criteria)
- Clear monitoring hooks in Console (per-connection TTF capture and sustained token/sec graphs)
- Amendment includes explicit limits: scoped to workspace DH-4093, 60-day review clause, and an uplift clause if usage exceeds the reserved profile.

If Product can provide signoff within 48 hours, treat this as "approved provisional" and we can present the amendment to Concord. Vanessa — push the intake form to Alice and ask them to confirm per-session vs per-tenant.

-Lauren

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Alice Cheng <alice@concordhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:42:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Streaming behaviour: TTF & sustained tokens — exception request

Alice — thanks for the quick response to my questions (see inline below).

We reviewed internally and can offer the following provisional amendment for the DH-4093 pilot workspace:

- Scoped commitment: TTF p95 <= 250ms for up to 10 concurrent streaming connections per workspace when using Redwood curated low-latency models.
- Sustained throughput: minimum 45 tokens/sec per active streaming connection under the reserved plan; if concurrency or aggregate throughput exceeds the reserved profile, Redwood will (a) throttle excess connections or (b) route overflow to the non-streaming sync endpoint with a documented token/sec expectation.
- Canary & monitoring: 14-day canary with synthetic probes; Redwood console will provide per-connection TTF and tokens/sec dashboards and anomaly alerts.
- Pricing: reserved-capacity uplift + monitoring surcharge (Rishi to share final figures).

Attached: concord_sla_amendment_draft.pdf (amendment template). If the terms above are acceptable, we’ll route a short DocuSign amendment and begin scheduling the canary once counters are in place.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Vanessa — thank you. The provisional amendment looks aligned with our needs. Confirming:

- The per-connection 45 tok/sec is what we require (each real-time session must meet that floor).
- We agree to the 14-day canary and the reserved plan pricing uplift.

Please send the DocuSign amendment and the canary playbook (metrics, probes, rollback steps). Legal copied here will review the final PDF.

We will target signature this week so we can start the pilot the following week.

Regards,

Concord Health
